# SDL3 generated byte contract and Windows checkout repair

Coordinator-reported ordinary native CI candidate `e223538` passes Linux x64/arm64 and macOS x64/arm64. Both Windows jobs fail `test_checked_in_contract_hashes_match_canonical_payloads` in the generator/build-contract test step. In the inspected workflow that gate precedes discovery/build/offline/audit steps. A failure there does not establish successful Windows artifact construction or linked execution, nor prove that an earlier linker problem recurred. Corrected Windows native execution remains pending coordinator rerun.

The reported digest pair reproduces exactly from the unchanged checked-in macOS x64 ledger:

| Physical payload bytes | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| UTF-8 with LF | `ae2a481830a8c42a5936ec79b37532ecd27f07fa2789ff395dd7c35173198829` |
| Same payload with CRLF line endings | `3339502cf5329b3d55cbb192d4a9531bb9ec719598e3d57daa7234ffdb3f230f` |

The inventory records the first digest and the unit test hashes physical `read_bytes()`. Git had no LF attributes for SDL3 assets, so `core.autocrlf=true` converted checkout bytes. The generator also used host-dependent `write_text()`, while its `read_text()` comparison hid CRLF differences through universal newline translation. This is a genuine generated-file storage/reproducibility defect, not incorrect API coverage or a reason to normalize away stale files in the test.

The repair defines exact UTF-8/LF bytes at both boundaries:

- Root `.gitattributes` applies `text eol=lf` only to the new `stdlib/Extensions/SDL3/*` module files, `tools/native/sdl3/inline-*.c`, `tools/native/sdl3/macros.c`, `tests/sdl3/layout-*.jai` and `tests/sdl3/c-layout-*.h`. This includes the generated module's license/notice assets used in byte-exact native package audits. SDL2, other Extensions, other native libraries and repository-wide file-type defaults are untouched. The ordinary SDL3 workflow watches `.gitattributes` changes.
- `sync_generated_file` encodes UTF-8 explicitly and reads/writes raw bytes. `--check` compares exact bytes and rejects CRLF, missing or modified assets. It does not rewrite, normalize, skip or accept stale files. Generation writes the same LF payload on Windows as elsewhere, and rejects any unexpected literal CR in generated data. Contract hashes retain their existing exact-byte meaning and values.
- SDL3 packaged third-party notices are written as explicit UTF-8 bytes, matching the checked-in LF asset. Notice source reads are explicitly UTF-8 and fail on malformed input rather than replacing data. All scanned pinned native source files were verified to decode as UTF-8. Native notice paths use forward slashes and case-sensitive component ordering, avoiding Windows path spelling/order differences. Copyright/license contents and generated notice payloads remain unchanged.

No Jai declaration, callback, enum, record layout, macro wrapper, core/GPU export, coverage ledger, inventory payload or stored contract hash changes in this repair. No platform hash exception, weakened assertion or ignored stale file is introduced.

Actual local verification (durable logs in `artifacts/sdl3/ci-e223538/`):

- Before the repair, a fresh isolated Git index with `core.autocrlf=true` reproduced the exact CRLF digest above (`regressions-before.log`). It uses only owned generated bytes and synthetic local paths, without other checkouts/history/user Git configuration or any remote. It is checkout evidence, not simulated native Windows execution.
- After the repair, 35 Python tests pass (`unit-final.log`). The Git regression verifies unchanged physical bytes across all scoped generated asset classes; a synthetic SDL2 path still converts to CRLF under Git's ordinary default, proving policy scope. Additional regressions reject stale CRLF and modified UTF-8 payloads, verify exact LF writes, and verify native notice paths/order. Existing all-six-profile contract hashes, full inventory and all 95 desktop GPU procedures remain checked.
- `python3 tools/sdl3_gen.py --source artifacts/sdl3/SDL3-3.4.18 --check` passes for all six targets with exact byte comparisons and wrapper compilation (`regeneration-final.log`). All generated sources, ledgers and hashes remain byte-identical to the preceding checkpoint. Python compilation of modified tools also passes.
- Local `python3 tools/sdl3_native.py --offline --jobs 2` and `python3 tools/test_sdl3.py --audit-only --platform macos-arm64 --native artifacts/native-libs/macos-arm64` pass (`native-host.log`, `audit-host.log`): real static/shared C smoke, pinned version, overflow wrappers, installed-header checks, 1,329 runtime exports including 95 GPU symbols, exact license/notices and artifact hashes. This is macOS arm64 execution only.

No Jai/Rust source changes here require a new formatter/linter result; prior actual strict lint and the unresolved real jaifmt POSIX dependency blocker remain documented in [formatting questions](../specs/questions/sdl3-formatting.md). Full integration and corrected Windows native jobs remain coordinator-owned. Rerun the ordinary six-target SDL3 workflow, retaining the generator/build-contract gate, real static/shared builds, offline rebuild and export/license audits. No workflow was dispatched, no issue comment posted, and release/publication stays held.
